summary: Outpost Zero is a mobile-friendly 3D educational game about managing a crewed Mars outpost. Each turn represents one Martian day, or sol. Players divide limited power among life support, radiation shielding, a greenhouse and solar repair. Their choices affect oxygen, food, radiation exposure, power capacity and crew health. Random events—including dust storms, solar flares, air leaks and crop blight—create changing priorities. Players aim to keep the crew alive for 20 sols until a resupply ship arrives. The game makes resource trade-offs and cascading consequences visible, helping students explore why maintaining a remote outpost requires balancing interconnected systems.
details:
The game shows outpost status meters and lets players adjust each system’s power allocation with touch-friendly controls. At the end of each sol, supplies and crew conditions change; the mission succeeds after 20 sols or fails if the crew cannot survive. The Mars scene responds visually to hazards, and multiplayer features show commanders online and share mission results.

It was developed with JavaScript ES modules, HTML, CSS, Three.js/WebGL and InstantDB. The environment, habitat model and audio were generated for the project; the resource rules are simplified, game-designed values—not a scientific simulation. The design emphasizes clear mobile controls, readable status indicators and the educational impact of decisions that affect more than one system.
